claim.claim-text: 1. A wireless device associated with a wireless network, the wireless device comprising:
one or more memories; and one or more processors coupled to the one or more memories, the one or more processors configured to cause:

generating a plurality of legacy fields and a plurality of non-legacy fields to form a frame, wherein the non-legacy fields comprise a first signal field, a second signal field and a data field, the first signal field comprising a bandwidth subfield to indicate an operating bandwidth of the frame and the operating bandwidth being divided into two or more 20MHz subchannels, the second signal field comprising user-specific information required to receive the frame, applying a first phase rotation value to each 20MHz subchannel of the first signal field, wherein the first phase rotation value is same for all subcarriers within a respective 20 MHz subchannel of the first signal field, applying a second phase rotation value to each 20MHz subchannel of the second signal field, wherein the second phase rotation value varies based on a group of subcarriers within a respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field, and transmitting the frame to one or more stations via the wireless network.

2. The wireless device of claim 1, wherein the second phase rotation value applied to a first group of subcarriers within the respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field is a first value, and the second phase rotation value applied to a second group of subcarriers within the respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field is a second value, the first value being phase-rotated by 180 degrees from the second value.

3. The wireless device of claim 2, wherein the first group of subcarriers to which the second phase rotation value is applied is a quarter of subcarriers in the respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field, and the second group of subcarriers to which the second phase rotation value is applied is three quarters of subcarriers in the respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field.
4. The wireless of claim 1, wherein the first phase rotation value is determined based on a position of the 20 MHz subchannel which the first signal field is associated with.

5. The wireless of claim 4, wherein the first phase rotation value applied to a 20 MHz subchannel which is lowest in frequency is 1, and the first phase rotation value applied to remaining 20 MHz subchannels is -1.
6. The wireless of claim 1, wherein the first signal field includes common control information commonly applied to the one or more stations.
7. The wireless of claim 1, wherein the user-specific information includes resource allocation for orthogonal frequency division multiple access, OFDMA, transmission.
8. A method performed by a wireless device associated with a wireless network, the method comprising:

receiving, through the wireless network, a frame comprising a plurality of legacy fields and a plurality of non-legacy fields, wherein the non-legacy fields comprise a first signal field, a second signal field and a data field, decoding the first signal field to obtain an operating bandwidth of the frame, the operating bandwidth being divided into two or more 20MHz subchannels, wherein each 20MHz subchannel of the first signal field is phase-rated by a first phase rotation value, the first phase rotation value being same for all subcarriers within a respective 20 MHz subchannel of the first signal field, decoding the second signal field to obtain user-specific information required to the wireless device to decode the frame, wherein each 20MHz subchannel of the second signal field is phase-rotated by a second phase rotation value, the second phase rotation value varying based on a group of subcarriers within a respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field, and decoding the data field using the first signal field and the second signal field.

9. The method of claim 8, wherein the second phase rotation value applied to a first group of subcarriers within the respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field is a first value, and the second phase rotation value applied to a second group of subcarriers within the respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field is a second value, the first value being phase-shifted by 180 degrees from the second value.

10. The method of claim 9, wherein the first group of subcarriers to which the second phase rotation value is applied is a quarter of subcarriers in the respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field, and the second group of subcarriers to which the second phase rotation value is applied is three quarters of subcarriers in the respective 20 MHz subchannel of the second signal field.
11. The method of claim 8, wherein the first phase rotation value is determined based on a position of the 20 MHz subchannel with which the first signal field is associated.

12. The method of claim 11, wherein the first phase rotation value applied to a 20 MHz subchannel which is lowest in frequency is 1, and the first phase rotation value applied to remaining 20 MHz subchannels is -1.

13. The method of claim 8, wherein the first signal field further comprises common control information commonly applied to the one or more stations, and the user-specific information includes resource allocation for orthogonal frequency division multiple access, OFDMA, transmission.
